summary: Sound, exactness-preserving and self-attributing (its own kernel name in the profile plus per-class PATH CHOSEN lines), so no companion is needed. The expected sizes are optimistic because the conversion moves onto SMSPs the consumers share rather than vanishing. One build-order change is mandatory before this scored run: as written, the bigger v3 build can push prepare past REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S=150 s and silently turn master's ft class OFF, which would regress the 138-weight first_turn shape.
justification: Mechanism: plausible. In master's dq_stage every lane re-converts its row-pair scales: per record it does 1 uint2 LDS and 2 cvt.f16x2.e4m3x2, and per k16 step it does __half22float2 (2 cvt), 2 FMUL by 2^119 and 2 __float2bfloat162_rn. That is about 6 instructions per k16 step plus 3 per record, roughly 54 per consumer warp per stage. The replacement costs 2 PRMT per k16 step plus the same one LDS (a uint4 now) per record. The uint4 at cw*128+g*16 is 4-lane broadcast over 128 contiguous bytes, so it is a single wavefront with no bank conflict. Exactness holds. e4m3 to f16 to f32 is exact, x2^119 stays in range (448*2^119 < FLT_MAX; the min subnormal 2^-9 becomes 2^110), and a 3-bit mantissa fits bf16, so the producer-computed bf16 values are bit-identical to what consumers build today. The smem math is also right: 211968 dynamic plus at most 14336 static (small class) plus 32 B of new barriers is under 232448, at 1 CTA/SM. Profile support: the rega pair is 381 us of 704 us (54%) on sliding turn_1 (w13 259.3, w2 122.1) and 1054 of 2098 us on sliding turn_4. The weight stream runs at about 2.1 TB/s of 4.8 at turn_1, and the 2-CTA/SM run gained on sliding turn_1, so consumer latency/issue is the limiter there. Direction: faster at turn_1, smaller at turn_4/ft. That is consistent with the weights, but the magnitudes are optimistic. WEAKEST LINK: 'producer warps 1-3 are idle' is true of the warps but not of the issue slots. Warps 1/2/3 sit on SMSPs 1/2/3, the same schedulers as two consumer warps each. A wgmma needs all four warps of a warpgroup, which spans all four SMSPs, so the slowest SMSP gates. Per stage the helpers add about 3 x (3 iterations x ~16 instr + wait/arrive) = 50-55 warp-instructions to SMSPs 1-3, and save about 2 x 36 = 72 there. So if rega is issue-bound, the net cut on the gating SMSPs is about 15-20 instructions per stage (a few %), not 25-30%. Only if it is latency-bound (the serialized dq_stage -> wgmma -> wait<0> chain) does the full ~36-instruction shortening of each consumer's critical path show up. That would be about 5-10% on w13/w2 at turn_1 and about 1-3% at turn_4/ft, so expect the low class, if anything, to clear the 0.98 gate, and turn_4/ft to land near it. The hypothesis also quotes turn_1 w13 at 283 us, but the current best profile shows 259.3 (sliding) and 226.4 (full). Its targets should be read against the profile's numbers. RISK TO MASTER (the scored-run concern): the BUILD section compiles _rega_src() plus the new string as ONE module, muse_prefill_rega_v3. That means 8 rega instantiations instead of 4, so nvcc goes from 38.6 s to roughly 65-80 s. In the master logs ft-self-check starts at about 119 s of prepare against REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S = 150 s. A 30-40 s longer build crosses that deadline, ft goes OFF ('prepare already used ... ft start deadline'), and first_turn falls back to Triton. Master's ft gate was 0.630, so that is about a 1.6x expert slowdown on every first_turn shape. 'Keep the new phases inside master's budget/deadline constants' is exactly what triggers it. Required fix: build master's v2 module UNCHANGED (same name, same source, same 38.6 s) and run master's whole setup including ft first. Then build ONLY the sx kernels (+ host entry rega_gemm_sx) as a separate small extension (e.g. muse_prefill_rega_sx_v1, prepended with _REGA_HEAD and the shared helpers so it shares no symbols at link time). Then run SX self-checks, the replay check and the gates under a separate SX deadline. A slow or failed SX build can then only cost SX, never master's ft. If the implementer keeps one module, they must at least raise REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S to cover the measured build delta and print it, but the separate-module order is strictly safer.
confounders: experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 / experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128: they define rega_kernel, the dq_stage being edited, the ring depth and the smem budget. They are the base, not a confound. The change is a strict sub-kernel edit with bit-identical outputs, and prepare gates SX against these exact kernels at the same T. Their prepare-time build sits on the critical path to the ft deadline, though (see justification).

align-two-phase-all-t-rega: decides the chunk/block tables the kernel walks, i.e. how many k-stages each CTA runs and how unbalanced they are. SX is gated and profiled on that same align, and the change is per-stage, so its relative effect does not depend on the align. Not a confound.

stack-tonight-five-prefill (align_par_ok / align2 precondition, router hi-lo) and experts-turn4-ssdq-s1b: rega wins the low/high gates, so ssdq and Marlin are untimed fallbacks. No interaction with the timed path.

Not landed but relevant for later: experts-rega-low-class-two-ctas-per-sm (neutral 1.4173, gained sliding turn_1). The +8 KB SX scale ring makes 2 CTAs/SM harder to fit, and both target the same turn_1 latency/issue slack, so their gains would overlap. Do not assume they add.
interference: No companion. Outputs are proven bit-identical in prepare, so every non-rega profile row should stay flat. SX is a distinct kernel symbol (rega_kernel_sx<G,BIG>), so the profile gives its µs per shape directly against the 259/122 (turn_1), 710/344 (turn_4) and ~3700/1850 (ft) master rows in FINDINGS. The prepare log prints per-class SX-vs-master graph medians and a PATH CHOSEN line. A headline gain or loss is therefore attributable from this one run: a loss is either the gate letting through a slower kernel (visible in the rows) or the ft-deadline failure above (visible as 'OFF ft'). A revert/tune companion would cost a second scored run without disambiguating anything the log does not already show. SIBLING experts-rega-pingpong-consumers-all-t: keep it SEPARATE, not stacked. Both edit consume_item's per-stage loop and both add 4 instantiations, so stacked they roughly double the build-time risk to the ft deadline. Their gains are sub-additive by design: ping-pong hides dequant under the other warpgroup's wgmma, which is exactly the time SX shortens. They add up only where dequant exceeds the wgmma time (the turn_1 low class at N 32/64). A stacked headline could not say which one moved. Stack afterwards as a third run, consume_item_pp calling the SX dq_stage, only if both clear their own class gates. Expect the stack to beat the better single one mainly at turn_1.
rules_flags: None blocking. Scales stay E4M3 bytes in global memory. The bf16 expansion lives only in per-stage shared memory inside one launch, the same values master already builds in registers. It is not a stored or cached weight copy and nothing is derived from inputs.

Keep kernel_fn dispatch on token-count class plus prepare flags only, with no prints, syncs or try/except. state['rega_sx'] must be per state copy (two prepared states), with no module or C++ static holding pointers or TMA maps. The hypothesis already says this, and the implementer should verify it.
Prepare time, not a rule but a scored-run hazard: the merged v3 build can trip REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S and disable master's ft class. Build SX as a separate extension AFTER master's ft setup.
open_questions: Print per SMSP-relevant counts if possible (ncu not available in judge). At minimum, print w13/w2 kernel-alone medians for both variants at each class gate T. If low-class SX is under 0.98 but turn_4/ft is flat, that confirms latency-bound at small N and issue/tensor-bound at large N.

Could warp 0 lanes 1-31 (idle beside the tid-0 producer) or a different helper distribution keep SMSP 1-3 load balanced? Or is a consumer-only cheaper conversion better? Example: build the bf16 scale straight from the e4m3 bits ((b & 0x7F) << 4 | sign), which is exactly e4m3 x 2^-120 for normals and subnormals alike, with the 2^-120 to 2^119 offset folded into the dequant8 code constant or the fp32 global scale. That would cut consumer scale work to about 2-3 integer ops per pair with no helpers, no extra smem and no extra barrier, but it changes dequant8's constant and needs its own exactness proof. A candidate follow-up if SX is flat.

Does the helper hop (wait full -> convert -> arrive sfull) ever run the ring dry at the start of a CTA's first item or after the epilogue barrier? Print the SX first-item latency, or compare a 1-item graph.
The hypothesis quotes turn_1 w13 at 283 us, but the current best profile shows 259.3 (sliding) and 226.4 (full). Re-anchor the expected targets to the profile before reading the result.
